title: A domain map with separable fraction fields is smooth on a principal open
statement: Let $R\to S$ be an injective finite type homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], where $R$ and $S$ are integral domains (nonzero rings in which a product is zero only if one factor is zero). Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$ be their fraction fields, the fields of fractions with nonzero denominators, with the induced embedding $K\to L$. If $L/K$ is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], then there exists $g\in S$, $g\ne0$, such that the composite $R\to S\to S_g$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Here $S_g$ is the ring of fractions $s/g^n$ for $s\in S$ and integers $n\ge0$, with the usual fraction operations.

source.place: Tag 07ND, lemma-smooth-at-generic-point, implication from separable fraction fields to smoothness at the zero prime; smoothness at that prime is expanded as the existence of a nonzero principal localization that is smooth.

proof.text: Write $\varphi:R\to S$ for the given map and $f:X=\operatorname{Spec}S\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for its spectrum morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The domain-spectrum statement [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] makes $Y$ integral. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] using the whole affine pair $X,Y$ and the given finite type ring map: $f$ is locally of finite type. It is also quasi-compact, as follows explicitly. Any affine open $V\subseteq Y$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Write $Y\setminus V=V(I)$; the opens $D(a)$ for $a\in I$ cover $V$, since a prime outside $V(I)$ omits some $a\in I$. Choose a finite subcover. The inverse image of each $D(a)$ is $D(\varphi(a))$, since the spectrum map contracts prime ideals. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] these inverse images are affine, hence quasi-compact by the same affine quasi-compactness statement. Their finite union is quasi-compact. Thus the hypotheses of generic local finite presentation hold.

source.place: Tags 01T1, 01T2 (finite type on affine charts); preparation for Tag 052A. Quasi-compactness expanded using basic opens.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation-lfp] to $f$. It gives a nonempty open $U\subseteq Y$ such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is locally of finite presentation. Choose $\mathfrak p\in U$ and write $Y\setminus U=V(J)$. Some $a\in J$ is absent from $\mathfrak p$, hence $a\ne0$ and $\mathfrak p\in D(a)\subseteq U$: any prime omitting $a$ cannot contain $J$. Put $b=\varphi(a)$. Injectivity gives $b\ne0$, and $f^{-1}(D(a))=D(b)$.

source.place: Tag 052A (proposition-generic-flatness), finite-presentation conclusion; the affine case is supplied by algebra.tex Tag 051T. This realizes the generic-finite-presentation reduction in Tag 07ND.

proof.text: The basic-open statement [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] identifies $D(a)$ and $D(b)$ with affine schemes having section rings $R_a$ and $S_b$, respectively, and identifies the induced ring map with the localization of $\varphi$. They are affine opens in $U$ and $f^{-1}(U)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to this affine pair for $f^{-1}(U)\to U$: $R_a\to S_b$ is of finite presentation. The map $R\to R_a$ has the explicit finite presentation $R[T]/(aT-1)\cong R_a$, sending $T$ to $1/a$; its inverse sends $r/a^n$ to $rT^n$ in the quotient. To check well-definedness, a fraction equality gives $a^k(a^m r-a^n s)=0$ for some $k\ge0$; multiplying this equality by $T^{k+m+n}$ in the quotient gives $rT^n=sT^m$. These maps preserve sums and products, and their composites fix $R$, $T$, and $1/a$, so are identities. This is a finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Composition in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] now gives that $R\to S_b$ is of finite presentation. Thus the first hypothesis of the local smooth-fibre criterion is available with the nonzero element $b\in S$.

source.place: Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), implication (1) to (2); algebra.tex Tags 00F3, 00F4. Explicit presentation for the base localization.

proof.text: Form $C=K\otimes_R S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible], applied using injectivity of $\varphi$, $C$ is a domain and is the localization of $S$ at the images of $R\setminus\{0\}$. The map $C\to L$ sends $\lambda\otimes s$ to $\lambda s$; in localization coordinates it sends $s/\varphi(r)$ to the same fraction in $L$, so is injective. Every element $s/t\in L$, with $s,t\in S$ and $t\ne0$, is the quotient of the images in $C$ of $s$ and $t$, so $L$ is also the fraction field of $C$. If $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ generate $S$ over $R$, their images generate $C$ over $K$, since every fraction $s/\varphi(r)$ is a polynomial in those images with coefficients in $K$. Hence $C$ is a finite type $K$-algebra. These identifications retain the given embedding $K\to L$ and its separability hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 07ND (lemma-smooth-at-generic-point), second paragraph: passage to the generic fibre. Fraction-field and finite-generation identifications written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-generic-point-over-field] with ground field $K$, finite type domain algebra $C$, and fraction field $L$. Step 4 verified the domain, finite type and fraction-field hypotheses, and $L/K$ is separable by assumption. Therefore $K\to C$ is smooth at its zero prime.

source.place: Tag 07ND, field-base case; equivalently Tag 00TV (lemma-separable-smooth) at the zero prime of the generic fibre.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q=(0)\subset S$. Its contraction is $\mathfrak p=(0)\subset R$ by injectivity. In [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], localization at zero in a domain inverts every nonzero element, so $R_{\mathfrak p}=\kappa(\mathfrak p)=K$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}=\kappa(\mathfrak q)=L$, compatibly with the induced local map. The map $K\to L$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. The fibre $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)=S\otimes_R K$ identifies with $C$ by $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes s$, with inverse $\lambda\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes\lambda$. The tensor balancing relations make both maps well defined, and multiplication of pure tensors shows that they are inverse $K$-algebra maps. Under this identification the map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)=L$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto s\lambda$, is exactly the injection of step 4, so its kernel, the corresponding prime $\mathfrak Q$, is zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime] to $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak q$: step 3 supplies $b\notin\mathfrak q$ with $S_b$ finitely presented over $R$, the local map is the flat field map just checked, and step 5 gives smoothness of the fibre at $\mathfrak Q$. Its conclusion is that $R\to S$ is smooth at $(0)$.

source.place: Tag 00TF (lemma-flat-fibre-smooth), with p=q=(0). This is the local fibre version of the reduction in Tag 07ND, whose comment explicitly permits 00TF in place of 00TG.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], smoothness at $\mathfrak q=(0)$ means that there is $g\in S\setminus(0)$ with $R\to S_g$ smooth. The condition $g\notin(0)$ is exactly $g\ne0$, so this is the required nonzero principal localization.

source.place: Tag 00TB (definition-smooth-at-prime), unpacked at the zero prime.
